answer: To resist sybil attacks an agent economy locks each new identity into a slow-melting glacier of non-transferable stake that only unlocks after 200 epochs of unique hardware-tied proofs. An attacker spinning up 500 clones must provision and maintain separate root keys for every clone, inflating the dune of ongoing verification cost linearly with identity count while a single honest agent incurs the cost once; any detected correlation burns the shared saffron-scarce residual collateral across the whole farm.
